title: Compactness heuristics and pool-harmony (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This note sketches a complementary set of heuristics and operational controls aimed at trading off compactness (how contiguous/live payloads are laid out) against latency and CPU cost of compaction in our KV cache. The goal is to reduce observable fragmentation that increases memory pressure and token-serving cost, while keeping tail latency and CPU budgets steady across tenants.

Context and motivation:
- We observe two sources of waste: (1) internal fragmentation from partially-used slots and headers, and (2) external fragmentation caused by uneven tenant allocations across slab/pool sizes. Existing work focuses on eviction policies and background compaction but lacks a measurable compactness objective and tenant-aware scheduling controls.

Goals:
- Define compactness metrics (operational and lightweight).
- Propose pool-harmony model: a cooperative rebalancer that moves minimal live payloads to improve contiguous free runs.
- Eviction & compaction coordination: how to prioritize eviction vs in-place compaction vs copy-compact.
- Controls: per-tenant compaction budgets, throttles, and safety knobs.

Key metrics:
- fragmentation_ratio = (allocated_bytes - live_payload_bytes) / allocated_bytes. Simple, recalculated per-shard every minute.
- contiguous_free_run_score: distribution histogram of consecutive free bytes per arena. We track p50/p95/p99 run sizes.
- compaction_efficiency = bytes_reclaimed / CPU_ms_spent_in_compaction.
- tenant_disruption_index: estimated additional tail-latency risk when migrating tenant entries (derived from request QPS and average latency sensitivity).

Pool-harmony model (high level):
- Pools are classified by slot-size class and NUMA-local arena. Each pool maintains a light-weight free-run index (LR-index) updated by alloc/free events.
- Harmony goal: keep at least one warm contiguous region per pool where large allocations can be satisfied without scattering. When pools fall below a target contiguous_free_run_threshold, they are candidates for harmony actions.

Harmony actions (ordered by cost):
1) Local recompact sweep: coalesce adjacent free slots by moving small live entries into neighbor slots in the same cache-line group. Low CPU, no cross-arena memory movement.
2) Slot shuffle within arena: pick low-traffic slots and migrate live payloads to form larger free runs. Uses a per-tenant disruption budget check.
3) Cross-pool migration: move small items from a high-fragmentation pool into a larger-slot pool (or vice versa) to defragment a targeted pool. Higher cost, higher impact.
4) Emergency bulk compact: a coordinated background job that temporarily pauses refill on a tenant to do high-throughput copy-compact of pages. Only used when fragmentation_ratio > emergency_threshold.

Eviction vs compaction coordination:
- Eviction is first-line for free space when under memory pressure. Compaction should be considered when eviction yields diminishing returns (eviction_recovery_curve flat) or when fragmentation_ratio is high but overall live_bytes still high.
- Heuristic to decide: compute projected_free_by_eviction for next N minutes based on tenant LRU skyline. If projected_free_by_eviction < needed_free_for_normal_routing AND fragmentation_ratio > frag_compact_threshold, schedule harmony actions.

Per-tenant controls and fairness:
- Each tenant has a compaction_budget (CPU_ms/minute) and migration_budget (bytes/minute). Harmony actions check both budgets before moving tenant entries. Budgets derived from tier: free, standard, enterprise.
- Soft-fairness: harmony scheduler uses weighted-round-robin across tenants where weights are a function of compaction_budget_remaining and tenant_allocated_bytes. This prevents a single noisy tenant from hogging compaction cycles.

Compaction scheduling and throttling:
- Background compactor runs as a multi-level worker pool: fast-local workers (low-latency friendly) and heavy-batch workers (high-throughput).
- Throttle signal inputs: overall CPU headroom, tail-latency SLOs (from tracing), tenant disruption index. If headroom drops below a threshold, only local recompact allowed.

Data movement primitives and optimizations:
- Copy-on-write with swap-pointer: allocate destination slot, write payload, then atomically swap slot pointer. Helps avoid inconsistent reads without global locks.
- In-place microcopy: for very small entries, use in-place bitshift/memmove in the same contiguous allocation to reduce pointer updates.
- Chunked migration: for large values, migrate in N sized chunks to avoid large spikes in bandwidth.

Observability and safety:
- Expose per-pool fragmentation_ratio, compaction_efficiency, and number of harmony actions in the last hour to Console dashboards.
- Add trace spans for each migration with tenant_id, bytes_moved, compaction_action_type.
- Safety: a migration abort path if a tenant experiences >Xms latency during migration (hook into tracing metrics).

Rollout plan (experimental phases):
1) Telemetry-only (2 weeks): collect compactness metrics, contiguous run stats, and per-tenant budgets without altering behavior.
2) Local recompact (4 weeks): enable local recompact sweep at 10% CPU budget globally; monitor compaction_efficiency and tail latency.
3) Slot shuffle & tenant budgets (6 weeks): enable slot-level migrations with per-tenant compaction budgets; gate cross-pool migration behind experiment flag.
4) Emergency bulk compact + policy tuning: enable emergency threshold and run a few maintenance windows to validate.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to measure and account for read amplification cost during migrations for persistent backing stores (if we spill)?
- Policy for metric decay: how long to keep a contiguous_run target after a pool receives heavy burst traffic?
- Should we expose per-tenant compaction budgets to customers as a configurable setting for Dedicated/Private deployments?
- Formalize safe concurrency model for pointer swap on 64-bit architectures with mixed language runtimes.

Next steps:
- Implement telemetry patch (INF-3421) and a small simulator that models harmony actions and projects compaction_efficiency.
- Run microbenchmarks for in-place microcopy vs copy-on-write for 64B-4KB payloads.
- Sync with SRE to define acceptable CPU headroom thresholds and targets for compaction_efficiency.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally a mid-level design: I want feedback on the pool-harmony action ordering and on the fairness/budget model. If we like it, we can convert into a formal spec with data structures and pseudocode.

---
End of draft.
